title: Psalms Bible Quiz - Chapter 57
description: Ten questions on Psalms 57: refuge under God's wings, a soul among lions, a net and a pit, and a heart that wakes the dawn with praise.

questions.text: In the shadow of what will the psalmist take refuge?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 57:1 he says that in the shadow of God's wings he will take refuge.

questions.text: Until when will the psalmist take refuge?
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:1 says he will take refuge until disaster has passed.

questions.text: What does verse 2 say God does for the psalmist?
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:2 speaks of God who accomplishes the psalmist's requests for him.

answers.text: He gives him a kingdom of his own
He hides him in a cave in the hills
He accomplishes his requests for him
He makes him rich in silver and gold

questions.text: What will God send out, according to verse 3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:3 says God will send out his loving kindness and his truth.

answers.text: His loving kindness and his truth

questions.text: Among what does the psalmist say his soul is?
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:4 says, "My soul is among lions."

questions.text: What are the teeth of the sons of men compared to in verse 4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:4 says their teeth are spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword.

questions.text: What have they prepared for the psalmist's steps?
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:6 says they have prepared a net for his steps.

questions.text: What happens to those who dig a pit before the psalmist?
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:6 says they fall into the middle of it themselves.

questions.text: Which instruments does the psalmist call to wake up?
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:8 says, "Wake up, lute and harp! I will wake up the dawn."

questions.text: How far does God's great loving kindness reach?
questions.explanation: Psalms 57:10 says God's loving kindness reaches to the heavens, and his truth to the skies.

answers.text: To the depths of the sea
To the ends of the mountains
To the gates of the city
